To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the locations of water pathways in PSII were determined by mapping the locations of oxidative modifications in PSII.

the locations of water channel(s) in the photosynthetic water oxidation complex, Photosystem II (the largest membrane protein complex), are revealed through the identification of reactive oxygen species damage sites on the lumen (stromal) side of the complex.

(i) we have identified 36 residues in the lumenal surface of PSII that are oxidized under physiological conditions; (ii) the residues that are oxidized cluster into three nearly continuous tracks, which we propose are water channels; (iii) we have identified the first oxidized residues in CP43, a protein that has been thought to have no function in oxygen evolution; and (iv) we have identified oxidized residues in the lutein-binding pocket of CP47,

our data provide a new insight into the structure of PSII, and in particular into the water channel in this complex.

we have identified three channels for water to pass through PSII.
the locations of water channel in PSII were revealed by the oxidized residues.

the locations of the oxidized residues on PSII are consistent with the locations of water channel in PSII, and the water channels in PSII are the most likely pathways that water molecules use to reach the catalytic Mn center.

the locations of oxidized residues can be used to map the locations of water molecules in the PSII structure, providing insight into the water channels within PS II that are essential to its function.
